I can never tell people enough of the importance of MULCH. Go into the forest and what do you see on the ground? Decaying leaves and branches. Lift up the forrest mulch and you will se a host of insects and worms. Beneath the mulch you will also find the richest soils. This process of decay not only blocks unwanted plants, it nourishes your plants all season. Don't try and re-invent mother nature, she already got it right. Happy gardening!

A boy plays toy cars with his little brother on the faded linoleum floor in the kitchen. There are a few spots, torn and jagged, that are held down with duct tape. As the oldest pulls his car along his duct tape driveway, an ear-shattering crash tears them away from their game.

Mom and Dad are fighting again.

Scared of their dad, but more for their mom, they peer into the next room.

"Stay away from me!" she screams as she throws another ashtray past their father's head. It smashes into pieces and falls to the floor. The two boys watch, completely shocked, as their dad lunges for their mom. He throws her to the ground. His hands wrap around her neck. Her screams become garbled and the boys watch.

Suddenly, the monster that used to be their dad turns around. It's eyes lock on them. Time stands still. Their father's eyes, usually a medium brown, are now black with rage. The whites of his eyes are completely visible all the way around that dark, hateful center.

Mom's hands flail. She breaks free somehow and rushes to the window. She leans her head out and screams, "Somebody call the police!"

The boys watch as she is pulled back in and thrown to the ground. The little brother rushes to his mom on the floor as the oldest watches, still frozen. A sharp kick and his little brother crumples, holding his ribs and crying.

Sirens in the distance.

The rage in the monster's eyes begins to fade as he walks back into the kitchen.

Police officers come inside wearing their dark black shirts with bright yellow badges, carrying shiny silver handcuffs. Their Dad screams that he's sorry as they take him away. That's the last time they ever see him.

Their grandparents come a little later to take the boys and their Mom to their house. It starts to rain a little as they carry their few suitcases and bags out to the van. After they climb in, they click their seat belts and look out the window to the only home they ever knew. Raindrops race down the window and the boys watch.
Holy shit, that was powerful. Well done.
